title: I can't code, so I decided to make my dream spaceship sandbox with ChatGPT. Here's KONTUR.
author: Vi----
selftext:

Hey guys! (English is not my first language, so sorry ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯ )

So, I'm basically a complete zero when it comes to coding. But I've spent hours playing games like Nimbatus, and Space Engineers, and Ressembly, I really liked them, but at the same time, something was missing. So, at some point I thought: why not try making my own ideal space-building game?

Meet **Kontur**, my little (well, not so little anymore) experiment.

It's a 2D spaceship-building sandbox with physics, engines, weapons, pistons, hinges, docking systems, logic, automation, factories and a whole bunch of other stuff too.  
  
But for me the best part is that by using Shells, you can give a building exactly the look, you want (yep, the ship designs in the screenshots are actually assembled from lots of tiny individual pieces).

And here's the funny part: **I haven't written the code myself.** ChatGPT does the programming, while I come up with ideas, design mechanics, test everything, find bugs, and try to explain to the AI what the hell went wrong this time.

It's definitely not a "made a game in 30 minutes" situation. We've gone through tons of attempts, broken things, fixed them, and occasionally broken them again.

Right now, my biggest headache is optimisation. I tried running 34 independently moving ships, and the FPS absolutely tanked. So that's our current engineering disaster to solve.

The game is still pretty rough, but it's slowly becoming something I'm genuinely happy with.

I'm planning to share a playable version after a few more updates. For now, I just wanted to show what I've managed to build with basically zero programming knowledge and a lot of motivation.

Would love to hear what you think, especially if you've tried something similar)
